I have waited for a good period of time to pass so I can write a full review of my installation using SolarBright. The system was installed back in Feb 2020. I had actually already committed to making the purchase a year earlier but chickened out.  Despite having put him through the 3rd degree, I wanted to wait til the system some friends had installed with Solar Bright had run for a while.He was an engineer but even that wasn't enough for me.So we ended up with 6.6kW system - 20 x 330w Seraphim panels and a Solax 5kW inverter. Cost: $4399.Yes - I have heard everything about Chinese v European panels and these are excellent...We live in Mollymook and so I was particularly concerned about installation and follow up service. It all went well although we waited a little longer perhaps than you may in the city but I knew in advance when they were coming and all was well.As you can imagine, I certainly also looked at many local providers because I did want to support local if I could.  To be frank those I dealt with were not always able to answer questions to my satisfaction and were without exception around a $1000 more expensive.Often there were sweeteners in there like systems to allow me to measure how much power I was saving or the sales line that xyz was a better panel, (without being able to quantify the difference) or that they would monitor the system for us .  But I think in the end a lot of it came down to the fact that they were all buying stock in smaller quantities so the unit price was more.Solar Bright imports the stock in significant quantities so there can be a significant price difference.We did have one issue with a gutter that was dislodged and, while the jury is out as to whether it was an effect of the installation SolarBright offered to pay for the fix. After the fires the gutter was also super heavy with ash and debris and there was a lot of rain so it could have been that too. But my point is their response.Having said that, I did find sometimes the admin side of the company lacked.  It could be that I needed more being regional or I am just a demanding client but I did have a couple of occasions when I had to chase down some information once I had finished dealing with Kevin.  But these were minor things.In the end, the system has worked flawlessly every day since then.Although we were receiving benefit from almost day 1 (after the final installation admin was completed) it was difficult to get a full comparison with previous years as we had changed retailers and also been away so used less power.However, between July & October 2019 and 2020, the bill halved from $474 to $210 with approximately the same usage.  A little more, in fact in 2020.The two bills since then in 2020 and 21 covering the warmer weather have both delivered credits of $84 and $118 respectively.Costs?  Not only the Solar but also as we had an old switchboard and both the units in our blocked shared one fuse there was extra electrical work.Still worth it?  Absolutely....
